standfirst: This issue covers Google's Gemini 4 Neon launch, ChatGPT for Accounting, new Claude Code releases, and tools you can try without an engineer.
digest: Google announced Gemini 4 Neon and opened Genie 4 to users, and Microsoft showed seven new models at Ignite. OpenAI added ChatGPT for Accounting and ChatGPT Wallet, which lets agents buy things with your approval. Claude Code 2.1.328 brought auto mode to Claude on Bedrock, Google Cloud and Foundry.

Gemini 4 Neon is the story clients are most likely to raise, since early commentary already compares it with Claude. Read the announcement and one hands-on opinion before you form a view. ChatGPT for Accounting matters if you advise finance teams that use QuickBooks, and the Claude Code change matters for clients who reach Claude through a cloud provider.

To try something this afternoon, n8n builds workflow automations visually, and ffmpeg-skill edits video on your own machine. Anthropic also priced its initial public offering this week, which clients may mention in passing. The KPMG audit trial report is worth a read before your next finance conversation.

items.title: Matt Wolfe rounds up 12 overlooked AI tools and demos
items.summary: Covers lifelike AI voices, interactive world models and new video editing tools. Good for spotting ideas to show clients, with no setup needed.

items.title: ChatGPT for Accounting drafts QuickBooks invoices from your email
items.summary: A demo of month-end close help: finding completed jobs in email, reconciling transactions and preparing reports. Relevant for finance clients using QuickBooks.

items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra rebuilds a 3D room from two video frames
items.summary: Shows Codex and Astra building a scene in Blender and turning it into an interactive space. Fun to watch, but aimed at technical users.

items.title: An OpenAI researcher uses ChatGPT to keep track of life admin
items.summary: A short clip on using ChatGPT to track details and make time for appointments. A quick idea to pass on to clients new to the tool.

items.title: Six people share underrated ways to use ChatGPT
items.summary: Short clip covering personal style, everyday logistics and stopping random subscription charges. Ideas to borrow for your own week.

items.title: Matt Wolfe's weekly recap covers Claude Fable 5.2 and Gemini 4 Carbon
items.summary: A rundown of one busy week, including new Claude and Gemini models, Adobe MAX features and Claude updates. Catch up in one sitting.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 builds slide decks and interactive explainers
items.summary: The presenter shows a deck made with Fable 5.2 and interactive lessons on winemaking and Central Park history. Useful if you build presentations.

items.title: Box CEO Aaron Levie on AI agents building business workflows
items.summary: An interview on why company data and context matter for agents, and how Box adapts as models change. Good background for client conversations.

items.title: Google DeepMind introduces Gemini 4 Neon
items.summary: Google's newest Gemini model, announced yesterday and heavily discussed on Hacker News. Check availability and pricing on the announcement page before a client asks.

items.title: Genie 4 is now available through Project Genie
items.summary: Google DeepMind opens Genie 4 to users through Project Genie. Quick to try if you want a feel for interactive world models.

items.title: Gemini app now runs on lower-memory Android devices
items.summary: Brings Gemini Live and custom image creation to cheaper phones. Worth knowing if your clients' staff use lower-end Android handsets.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.328 adds auto mode on Bedrock, Google Cloud and Foundry
items.summary: Also adds a block option for failing MCP tool hooks. Relevant if clients run Claude through a cloud provider; update as usual.

items.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets agents buy things with your approval
items.summary: Agents in ChatGPT Work, Codex and dots can complete purchases using existing card protections. Check approval settings before letting staff try it.

items.title: Microsoft announces seven new models at Ignite 2026
items.summary: Pitched on price and performance, with a 510-point Hacker News thread behind it. Worth skimming if your clients are Microsoft shops.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.323 adds an experimental Code Mode
items.summary: Code Mode has Claude write JavaScript to call its tools, and it is opt-in. Organizations can switch it off, so check before rolling out.

sections.title: Tools and skills you can use

items.title: n8n automates workflows with 400+ integrations and AI steps
items.summary: A visual workflow builder you can host yourself or use in the cloud. Good for scheduled automations, though self-hosting needs IT help.

items.title: ffmpeg-skill gives coding agents 42 local video editing tools
items.summary: Cuts, captions, reframing and platform exports run on your machine with no cloud or API keys. Needs Claude Code or a similar agent.

items.title: video-shotcraft makes editable product promo videos in Claude Code
items.summary: A skill with 124 shot recipes, beat sync and sound design, built on Remotion. Handy for client demos, but expect some tinkering.

items.title: Google's stitch-skills add design skills for the Stitch MCP server
items.summary: A library of skills that works with Claude Code and other agents once Stitch is connected. Setting up the connection is the hard part.

items.title: Plannotator lets you annotate agent plans and send feedback in one click
items.summary: A workspace for reviewing what an agent plans to do and sharing comments with your team. Useful if you supervise agent work.

items.title: Sellbird runs cold email outreach on your Claude or ChatGPT plan
items.summary: Open source platform that finds contacts, verifies emails, writes messages and handles replies. Check client consent and sending rules before you try it.

items.title: Dodaios puts Claude Code, Codex and seven more agents in one workspace
items.summary: Open source app that runs on your own plans and keys, with voice and docs included. A quick way to compare agents side by side.

items.title: AI agents ask better questions than KPMG accountants in audit trial
items.summary: A trade-press report on an audit trial with a busy 189-comment Hacker News thread. Useful for finance clients asking where agents help.

items.title: Sumitomo Life's leaders drove ChatGPT Enterprise adoption by using it first
items.summary: A vendor customer story on insurer research, proposals and investment analysis code. Early executive use drove uptake, a pattern worth borrowing for rollouts.

items.title: Gemini 4 Neon looks like an Opus 5.5 competitor, one blogger argues
items.summary: A hands-on opinion with 208 points and 67 comments. Read the thread for how people compare the new model with Claude.

items.title: Inside the Codex sandbox explains how filesystem and network limits work
items.summary: OpenAI explains how Codex enforces the limits you set across macOS, Linux and Windows. Useful for answering client security questions about coding agents.

items.title: Holiday Extras' dots deliver reports and flag issues unprompted
items.summary: A customer story about assistants that send launch reports and brief people on upcoming meetings. Shows what proactive agents look like at work.

items.title: OpenAI surveys 1,800 scientists on how they use ChatGPT
items.summary: Findings on daily workflows and reported productivity. Vendor-run, but a useful reference for how professionals say they use it.
